text: At a sports event, a champion runner and a car take part in a race.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State the form of energy gained by the train as it begins to move.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: The train travels a distance of 4.0 km along a straight, horizontal track.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Calculate the work done on the train during this part of the journey.
work done = ______

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The mass of the train is 450 000 kg.
Calculate the maximum possible speed of the train at the end of the first 4.0 km of the
journey.
maximum possible speed = ______

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
In practice, the speed of the train is much less than the value calculated in (ii).
Suggest one reason why this is the case.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
After travelling 4.0 km, the train reaches its maximum speed. It continues at this constant
speed on the next section of the track where the track follows a curve which is part of a circle.
State the direction of the resultant force on the train as it follows the curved path.

text: An electric train is initially at rest at a railway station. The motor causes a constant force of
360 000 N to act on the train and the train begins to move.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The boxes on the left contain the names of some sources of energy. The boxes on the right
contain properties of some sources of energy.
Draw two straight lines from each box on the left to the two boxes on the right which describe
that source of energy.
renewable
solar energy
not renewable
polluting
natural gas
not polluting

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Coal-fired power stations are polluting.
State an advantage of using coal as a source of energy.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A coal-fired power station generates electricity at night when it is not needed.
Some of this energy is stored by pumping water up to a mountain lake. When there is high
demand for electricity, the water is allowed to flow back through turbines to generate electricity.
On one occasion, 2.05 × 10 kg of water is pumped up through a vertical height of 500 m.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Calculate the weight of the water.
weight = ______

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained by the water.
energy gained = ______

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
The electrical energy used to pump the water up to the mountain lake is 1.2 × 10 J.
Only 6.2 × 10 J of electrical energy is generated when the water is released.
Calculate the efficiency of this energy storage scheme.
efficiency = ______

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by a linear scale.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The highest temperature that this thermometer can measure is 110 °C.
State the lowest temperature that it can measure.
lowest temperature = ______

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A second liquid-in-glass thermometer has the same range but it has a greater sensitivity.
Suggest two ways in which the second thermometer might differ from the first.
1. ______
2. ______

parts.text:
A thermometer has a bulb that is painted white and is shiny.
It is placed in boiling water for several minutes. It is then removed from the water and is held
in air.
Fig. 4.1 shows how the thermometer reading changes during the next 8 minutes.

The procedure is repeated.

parts.text:
On Fig. 4.1, sketch a second line to suggest how the reading of the re-painted
thermometer changes during the 8 minutes.

parts.label: (ii)

text: A liquid-in-glass thermometer has a linear scale and a range of 120 °C.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the specific latent heat of fusion (melting) of a substance.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Ice cubes of total mass 70 g, and at 0 °C, are put into a drink of lemonade of mass 300 g.
All the ice melts as 23 500 J of thermal energy transfers from the lemonade to the ice. The
final temperature of the drink is 0 °C.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Calculate the specific latent heat of fusion for ice.
specific latent heat of fusion = ______

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The thermal energy that causes the ice to melt is transferred from the lemonade as
it cools. The loss of this thermal energy causes the temperature of the 300 g of the
lemonade to fall by 19 °C.
Calculate the specific heat capacity of the lemonade.
specific heat capacity = ______

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
The melting ice floats on top of the lemonade.
Explain the process by which the lemonade at the bottom of the drink becomes cold.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: A sound wave in air consists of alternate compressions and rarefactions along its path.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain how a compression differs from a rarefaction.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
Explain, in terms of compressions, what is meant by
1. the wavelength of the sound,

2. the frequency of the sound.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
At night, bats emit pulses of sound to detect obstacles and prey. The speed of sound in air is
340 m / s.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
A bat emits a pulse of sound of wavelength 0.0085 m.
Calculate the frequency of the sound.
frequency = ______

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: State why this sound cannot be heard by human beings.

parts.label: (iii)
parts.text:
The pulse of sound hits a stationary object and is reflected back to the bat. The pulse is
received by the bat 0.12 s after it was emitted.
Calculate the distance travelled by the pulse of sound during this time.
distance = ______

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A student determines the resistance of a length of aluminium wire.
She connects the wire in series with a battery and a variable resistor. The circuit is shown in
Fig. 8.1.
aluminium wire
Fig. 8.1
She knows that an ammeter and a voltmeter are needed in the circuit.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: On Fig. 8.1, draw the circuit symbol for an ammeter connected in a suitable position.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
A variable resistor is included so that the current in the circuit may be changed.
Suggest an advantage of being able to change the current.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Electricity is transmitted from a power station to a distant city using an aluminium cable of
resistance 1.2Ω. Power loss occurs because of the resistance of the cable.
The current in the cable is 250 A.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Calculate the power loss in the cable.
power loss = ______

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
The aluminium cable is replaced with a new aluminium cable of the same length. The
current remains at 250 A. The diameter of the new cable is double the diameter of the
original cable.
State and explain how the power loss is affected by this change.

parts.text: Name the type of nuclear reaction taking place in the Sun.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Many of the charged particles produced by the Sun are emitted from its surface at high
speeds and travel out into space.

parts.label: (i)
parts.text: Explain why these particles constitute an electric current.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text:
State the equation that relates the electric current I to the charge Q that is flowing. Define
any other terms in the equation.

parts.text:
Some of the particles emitted by the Sun travel straight towards the Earth until they enter the
Earth’s magnetic field. Because they constitute a current, they experience a force and are
deflected.

1. the direction of the current,

2. the direction of the magnetic field.
